data.title: A decade of discovery
data.description: Big Bad Wolf Books is celebrating its 10th anniversary in Thailand with a series of book sales across the country.

data.title: Paramount settles with US states to clear Warner Bros. mega-merger
data.description: LOS ANGELES (UNITED STATES) - Paramount has reached a settlement with a group of US states that clears the way for its takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, US media reported Monday, creating a Hollywood empire spanning television, news and cinema.

data.title: British Museum bans photos of Bayeux Tapestry as crowds linger
data.description: LONDON - The British Museum has banned visitors from taking pictures of the Bayeux Tapestry in order to keep the crowds flowing through an unprecedented London exhibition, a spokesperson confirmed Monday.

data.title: Asean Cup: Stars report for training
data.description: Thailand's national team have reported for a training camp ahead of the Fifa Asean Cup 2026 in Indonesia, with head coach Anthony Hudson bringing together a squad built around senior figures.

data.title: Buriram go top as own goal sinks Sharks
data.description: Buriram United moved to the top of the Thai League 1 table on Sunday night, edging out hosts Chonburi 1-0 in a tense encounter at Chonburi Stadium.

data.title: Upper House debates law changes report
data.description: The Senate on Monday debated a report proposing changes to election laws and the constitution, including reforms to the Election Commission (EC).

data.title: Natthaphong accepts PAO poll defeat
data.description: People's Party (PP) leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut has accepted the party's defeat in the Nonthaburi Provincial Administrative Organisation (PAO) chief election, saying he had no regrets about fielding Decharut Sukkumnoed.

data.title: PP to submit Senate vote collusion 'evidence'
data.description: People's Party (PP) leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut said on Monday the party would submit evidence to the National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC) by Friday over alleged collusion in the 2024 Senate election.

data.title: Anutin says cabinet has no ties to grey businesses
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul insisted on Monday that no member of his cabinet has ties to grey or illicit businesses and that his government has no reason to compromise with anyone involved in illegal activities.

data.title: PP slams co-payment scheme
data.description: People's Party (PP) deputy leader Sirikanya Tansakun on Monday criticised the planned second phase of the "Thais Help Thais Plus" co-payment scheme, saying it was too small to stimulate the economy or adequately ease the burden of rising living costs.

data.title: Senators query EC after names appear in probe files
data.description: A group of senators calling themselves New Breed senators have questioned the Election Commission (EC) over complaints against them after finding their names in separate investigation files.

data.title: PM 'must explain rejections'
data.description: Opposition leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut has questioned Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul over the rejection of four citizen-backed bills involving financial matters, arguing the proposed legislation would have benefited the public.

data.title: DSI to forward Forex-3D scam dossier to prosecutors
data.description: The Department of Special Investigation (DSI) is expected to forward its completed case file in the high-profile Forex-3D investment fraud investigation to public prosecutors this week.

data.title: Infantino proposes consulting federations to reform FIFA
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - FIFA president Gianni Infantino on Monday suggested a "consultation" with the member federations to reform the world football governing body's decision-making processes, in a letter addressed to the 211 member associations, and seen by AFP.

data.title: Farmers oppose seed changes
data.description: Farmer groups and their civil society allies will gather at the Agriculture Ministry on Wednesday to oppose draft legal changes that would align Thailand with an international convention granting plant breeders stronger intellectual property rights over new seed varieties.

data.title: Ja Thawee dies at age 92
data.description: Thawee Buranakhet, better known as Ja Thawee, a National Artist renowned for his sculpture and bronze casting, has died at the age of 92.

data.title: Free MRT rides for bike, e-scooter users
data.description: Passengers travelling with bicycles or foldable electric scooters will be able to use the MRT network for free today as part of World Car Free Day 2026.

data.title: Seniors urged to use traditional Chinese medicine  to slow cognitive decline
data.description: Older people are being encouraged to adopt four daily practices based on traditional Chinese medicine to help maintain brain health and slow cognitive decline.

data.title: Air hostess heroin case advances
data.description: The Office of the Attorney-General (OAG) has ordered the indictment of four suspects allegedly linked to a transnational drug trafficking network involving Thai Airways flight attendant Meena Kondo in a heroin smuggling case.

data.title: Amnesty panel sets out process
data.description: A new committee tasked with promoting social peace will push ahead with an amnesty process aimed at ending political conflicts that have persisted for more than two decades, said Deputy Prime Minister Pakorn Nilprapunt.

data.title: Democrats petition for audit of TH-AI Passport
data.description: The Democrat Party on Monday petitioned the Auditor-General to investigate the 1.621-billion-baht TH-AI Passport project, raising seven concerns over procurement, payment criteria, AI performance, project targets and data governance.

data.title: Navy commander defends frigate bid
data.description: Navy Commander‑in‑Chief Adm Pairoj Fuangchan said on Monday that the bidding process for a new naval frigate was transparent and that the navy has no concerns about scrutiny of its procurement process.

data.title: MRT Blue Line back to normal
data.description: Normal MRT Blue Line services resumed Monday morning after an electrical fault near Tao Poon station damaged power and signalling equipment and disrupted services on Sunday.

data.title: Govt racing to conclude US tariff negotiations
data.description: Thailand is seeking to conclude trade negotiations with the United States before Washington announces the results of investigations into Thai trade practices that could lead to additional tariffs, Deputy Prime Minister and Commerce Minister Suphajee Suthumpun said.

data.title: PM eyes stronger Japan ties
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul on Monday urged Thailand and Japan to move from producing goods for one another to producing them together, saying closer supply-chain ties would help sustain Japanese investment as the automotive industry shifts towards electric vehicles.

data.title: El Nino weather pattern enters record territory: scientist
data.description: NEW YORK - The strengthening El Nino weather pattern has tied for the most intense on record on a widely-used metric, a senior scientist told AFP Monday, even as its influence is already being felt from Central America to Indonesia.

data.title: Man shot by ICE agent in Texas detained with bullet inside him: lawyer
data.description: AUSTIN - A Venezuelan national shot and wounded by a US immigration agent in Texas was jailed with the bullet still inside his body, his lawyer said Monday.

data.title: South African ostriches plucked alive for luxury fashion: report
data.description: JOHANNESBURG - South African ostrich farms are using mechanical pluckers to remove feathers from living birds destined for major luxury fashion brands in techniques that are cruel and painful, animal welfare group World Animal Protection said on Monday.

data.title: US media outlets to sue Trump administration after White House ban
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Three leading US news outlets announced Monday they will go to court after being banned from the White House, as President Donald Trump claimed that media critical of his administration is a "Cancer" threatening national security.

data.title: German auto workers stage mass protests in bid to save jobs
data.description: HANOVER (GERMANY) - German automotive workers held nationwide protests on Monday calling for government and management action to protect jobs and factories in an industry facing severe headwinds.

data.title: Supply issues, attacks on refineries driving diesel prices upward
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Prices at the pump for diesel and other fuels are hitting fresh highs in many countries as the wars and the Middle East and Ukraine have not only choked off crude supplies, but also damaged refineries, with the resulting capacity constraints increasingly being felt, according to analysis out of France.

data.title: COP31 host says AI's climate footprint to be a summit priority
data.description: NEW YORK - COP31 host Turkey said Monday that pursuing "climate-responsible AI" and pushing tech companies to power data centers with clean energy would be priorities when it stages next month's summit.

data.title: Renewables hit record in 2025, but world must move faster: report
data.description: NEW YORK - A new report has shown global renewable power capacity grew by record levels last year, with the findings hailed as a sign by the UN climate chief that the "brute power of market forces" is making the transition to clean energy irreversible.

data.title: Merz vows to keep ruling coalition together for 'democratic future' of Germany
data.description: BERLIN - Chancellor Friedrich Merz vowed Monday to keep his ruling coalition together for the sake of Germany's "democratic future" after crushing defeats in two regional elections fuelled speculation about his future.

data.title: Schoolgirl Yu scorches to second gold as doping case rocks Asian Games
data.description: NAGOYA (JAPAN) - Schoolgirl swimmer Yu Zidi won her second gold of the Asian Games on Monday with the fastest time in the world this year, while a teenage badminton player became the first doping case.
